news.title: 'We never gave up, and that's the best message we could send': Scaloni looks beyond tough World Cup
news.lede: Lionel Scaloni believes Argentina’s run to the 2026 World Cup final demanded more from his team than their previous triumph in Qatar, with injuries and fitness issues forcing difficult decisions along the way. Now, with the tournament behind them, the Argentina coach wants to use the next phase to introduce younger players without losing the spirit that has carried the team through an extraordinary eight-year cycle. Speaking to Asian channel MiGu, Scaloni revealed that Argentina arrived in the United States in considerably worse physical condition than they had in Qatar. “We arrived at the previous World Cup (2022) in much better shape, with 95% of the players at their best; this time we arrived with just enough,” Scaloni said.

news.title: Russia handed partial international football return as FIFA includes youth team in Under-15 World Cup draw
news.lede: Youth squad enters tournamentRussia have officially returned to the international football fold at youth level after being included in the group-stage draw for the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan. Placed in a six-team pool alongside Turkey, Afghanistan, Djibouti, Sierra Leone, and Sudan, the decision marks the first easing of sporting sanctions against the nation since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Explaining the central purpose behind launching the pilot competition, FIFA stated: "The FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival addresses a fundamental challenge in international football: providing meaningful competitive opportunities for nations in which qualifying for FIFA competitions remains an enormous challenge."

news.title: FIFA Boss Gianni Infantino in Danger of Losing Job? Greek FA President Wants Change at Top
news.lede: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino is hoping to be re-elected in 2027 but may have just received a hard hit as the Greek FA president Makis Gagatsis along with Oliver Bierhoff, who was Germany's team director for 18 years, have called for a change in leadership. news.title: Falconets Receive Huge Warning About Colombia's Credentials At FIFA Women's World Cup
news.lede: Nigeria’s female youth national team, Falconets have received a huge warning that they will not find the going easy when they face Colombia in the quarter-finals of the ongoing FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, Sports247 reports. The warning comes with a reminder that the South Americans are into the competition’s quarter-finals for a second consecutive edition, though they progressed from Group E of this year’s championship as a third-placed team. With their sudden burst of form turning out to be good enough, Moses Aduku’s squad will have to redouble their efforts in order to overcome the Colombians, who reached the last eight after edging hosts Poland 1-0 on Thursday.

news.title: VAR under scrutiny as technology’s role in football expands
news.lede: Another domestic football season is underway, and already, in mid-September, the shortcomings of technology in sport are at the centre of the discourse once again. The video assistant referee (VAR) is perhaps the most discussed technology in modern sport. While video replays have been in use for years in sports like American football, rugby or cricket, it has only been a decade since the International Football Association Board (IFAB), the highest regulatory authority in the sport, approved the use of VAR. With artificial intelligence (AI) reportedly reaching dangerous levels of development and technological optimisation of people's lives at an all-time high, it is perhaps a pertinent time to consider the use of technology in sport.
